groups.Cat: Look at fur colour, markings, ear shape and tail. Coat patterns are not the same as breeds.
groups.Dog: Look at size, ear shape, coat and muzzle. Many dogs are mixes and cannot be identified by looks alone.
groups.Snail: Check the shell shape, colour, bands and habitat. Never pull a snail off a surface.
groups.Butterfly: Notice wing colour and patterns on both sides. Photograph butterflies without catching them.
groups.Moth: Moths vary widely in shape and colour. Some fly by day; look at wing patterns and antennae.
groups.Bee: Notice body shape, hairiness and markings. Watch bees from a distance and leave flowers undisturbed.
groups.Ladybird: Count spots only as one clue. Pattern, size and head markings can matter more.
groups.Beetle: Beetles have hard wing cases. Look at body shape, antennae and colours.
groups.Dragonfly: Dragonflies have four long wings and large eyes. Check abdomen shape, colour and habitat.
groups.Ant: Ants have elbowed antennae and narrow waists. Colours vary; many look alike.
groups.Spider: Spiders have eight legs and no antennae. Look at their web, markings and body shape.
groups.Bird: Look at beak, size, wing bars and tail as well as colour. Listen for calls without approaching nests.
groups.Squirrel: Look at ears, tail, size and coat colour. Coat colours can vary within a species.
groups.Rabbit: Wild rabbits and pet rabbit breeds can look different. Look at ear shape, size and setting.
groups.Hedgehog: Look for a rounded body, pointed snout and spines. Observe without touching or disturbing it.
groups.Frog: Look at skin, colour, leg length and habitat. Patterns vary and some species are hard to distinguish.
groups.Other: For an unfamiliar animal, photograph it safely and record where you saw it. It is fine to say “Not sure”.

Cat.Tabby: Often has stripes, swirls or spots; look for the M-shaped mark on the forehead.
Cat.Ginger: Orange or reddish coat; many ginger cats also show faint or bold tabby stripes.
Cat.Brown: A brown coat can be solid or patterned; check whether stripes are visible.
Cat.Black: Looks mostly black, though sunlight may reveal faint markings.
Cat.White: Mostly white fur; eye colour can be blue, green, amber or mixed.
Cat.Cream: Pale warm beige colouring; compare with the deeper orange of ginger.
Cat.Tuxedo: Usually black with white on the chest, paws or face, like a little suit.
Cat.Calico: Distinct areas of white, orange and dark fur; a coat pattern, not a breed.
Cat.Tortoiseshell: Mottled black and orange or brown patches, usually with very little white.
Cat.Grey: Cool grey or blue-looking coat; may be solid or tabby-patterned.
Cat.Colourpoint: Paler body with darker ears, face, paws and tail.
Cat.Other: If the markings do not fit, describe the colours and pattern in your notes.

Dog.Labrador: Sturdy body, short dense coat and broad head; black, yellow or chocolate are common.
Dog.Golden Retriever: Medium-large dog with a feathered golden coat and hanging ears.
Dog.Poodle: Curly coat, narrow muzzle and long legs; sizes vary widely.
Dog.Terrier: Often lively-looking with a wiry or smooth coat; many different terrier breeds exist.
Dog.Spaniel: Usually has soft floppy ears and a silky or wavy coat.
Dog.Bulldog: Stocky build, broad head, short muzzle and skin folds.
Dog.Dachshund: Long body, short legs and drooping ears.
Dog.Husky: Thick double coat, upright ears and bushy tail; eyes may be blue or brown.
Dog.Mixed Breed: A mixed-breed dog may combine features of several breeds; looks alone cannot confirm ancestry.

Snail.Garden Snail: Rounded brown shell often with flecks or mottling; typically found in damp gardens.
Snail.Grove Snail: Smooth shell may be yellow, pinkish or brown, sometimes with dark spiral bands.
Snail.Roman Snail: A relatively large, rounded, pale shell with many visible growth lines.
Snail.Glass Snail: Thin, glossy, often translucent shell; the body may be visible through it.
Snail.Amber Snail: Small amber-coloured shell with a large opening, often near damp plants.
Snail.Pond Snail: Aquatic snail with a taller pointed shell, typically in fresh water.
Snail.Other Snail: Check shell shape and location; different species can look very similar.

Butterfly.Peacock: A large eye-shaped spot on each reddish-brown wing is the key clue.
Butterfly.Red Admiral: Dark wings with bright red-orange bands and white markings near the tips.
Butterfly.Small Tortoiseshell: Orange wings with black and yellow patches and blue crescents at the edges.
Butterfly.Painted Lady: Orange and brown wings with black tips and small white spots.
Butterfly.Comma: Orange-brown wings with deeply scalloped edges; the underside has a tiny white C mark.
Butterfly.Large White: Mainly white wings with dark tips and sometimes black spots.
Butterfly.Common Blue: Males often look bright blue above; females are usually brown with orange edge spots.
Butterfly.Brimstone: Leaf-shaped, pale yellow-green wings; females are often paler.

Moth.Emperor Moth: Large furry moth with bold round eye-spots on each wing.
Moth.Elephant Hawk-moth: Often pink and olive green, with a streamlined body.
Moth.Hummingbird Hawk-moth: Hovers in front of flowers and has orange hindwings.
Moth.Garden Tiger: Bold cream-and-brown forewings, often with bright orange hindwings.
Moth.Jersey Tiger: Dark forewings with creamy stripes and bright orange or red hindwings.
Moth.Six-spot Burnet: Dark iridescent wings with pairs of red spots; often found on flowers.
Moth.Silver Y: Mottled grey-brown forewings with a small silver Y-shaped marking.

Bee.Honeybee: Brown-and-gold banded abdomen and slimmer shape than many bumblebees.
Bee.Buff-tailed Bumblebee: Rounded, furry bee with yellow bands and a pale buff or off-white tail.
Bee.Red-tailed Bumblebee: Black fuzzy body with a rusty red or orange tail.
Bee.White-tailed Bumblebee: Black-and-yellow bands with a clean-looking white tail.
Bee.Common Carder Bee: Ginger or brown furry thorax; banding can be subtle.
Bee.Leafcutter Bee: Often carries pollen on hairs under the abdomen and cuts neat circles from leaves.
Bee.Mining Bee: Many species nest in soil; often furry, small to medium, and hard to distinguish.

Ladybird.Seven-spot: Typically red with seven black spots; three on each wing case and one by the centre.
Ladybird.Two-spot: Often red with two black spots, but darker forms also exist.
Ladybird.Harlequin: Highly variable colours; often a pale W-shaped marking behind the head.
Ladybird.Fourteen-spot: Usually yellow with rectangular black markings that can merge into a checkerboard.
Ladybird.Pine Ladybird: Mostly dark with red spots shaped a little like commas.
Ladybird.Twenty-two-spot: Bright yellow with many small black spots; usually found near mildew.

Beetle.Stag Beetle: Large beetle; males have antler-like jaws, while females have smaller jaws.
Beetle.Rose Chafer: Shiny metallic green beetle, often seen feeding on flowers.
Beetle.Ground Beetle: Often dark, fast-running and found beneath stones or logs.
Beetle.Weevil: Many have a long snout with antennae set partway along it.
Beetle.Soldier Beetle: Soft-looking, elongated body; often red or orange on summer flowers.
Beetle.Click Beetle: Long narrow body; can make a click to spring itself upright.
Beetle.Longhorn Beetle: Often has antennae as long as, or longer than, its body.
Beetle.Dung Beetle: Often rounded, sturdy and found around animal dung.

Dragonfly.Emperor Dragonfly: Large dragonfly with vivid blue abdomen and green thorax, especially in males.
Dragonfly.Broad-bodied Chaser: A broad, flattened abdomen; mature males often look powdery blue.
Dragonfly.Southern Hawker: Large patterned dragonfly; males show blue and green markings.
Dragonfly.Common Darter: Small dragonfly that often perches; mature males are frequently reddish.
Dragonfly.Four-spotted Chaser: Look for four distinct dark spots near the middle of the wings.
Dragonfly.Golden-ringed Dragonfly: Very long black-and-yellow ringed body and green eyes.

Ant.Black Garden Ant: Small, dark brown or black ant commonly seen on paths and in gardens.
Ant.Red Ant: Often reddish with a darker abdomen; several different species share this name.
Ant.Wood Ant: Usually reddish-brown and dark, often near large mound nests in woodland.
Ant.Yellow Meadow Ant: Small yellowish ant that spends much of its life underground.
Ant.Pavement Ant: Tiny dark ants often nesting in cracks between stones.
Ant.Other Ant: Look at size, colour and nesting place; close-up details may be needed.

Spider.Garden Spider: Rounded abdomen with a pale cross-shaped pattern; often in circular webs.
Spider.House Spider: Long-legged brown spider; many species occur inside buildings.
Spider.Jumping Spider: Compact body and very large front-facing eyes; moves in short jumps.
Spider.Zebra Spider: Tiny jumping spider with clear black-and-white stripes.
Spider.Wolf Spider: Fast ground hunter with a robust body, often seen without a web.
Spider.Crab Spider: Front legs held sideways like a crab; often waits on flowers.
Spider.Cellar Spider: Very long thin legs and a small body; often hangs upside down indoors.

Bird.Robin: Orange-red face and chest, with a brown back; often hops near gardens.
Bird.Blackbird: Adult males are black with a yellow-orange bill; females are browner.
Bird.House Sparrow: Small, chunky brown bird; adult males have a grey crown and black throat.
Bird.Blue Tit: Blue cap, yellow underside and white cheeks with a dark eye stripe.
Bird.Great Tit: Black head with white cheeks and a central black stripe on a yellow belly.
Bird.Magpie: Long tail and bold black-and-white body with an iridescent sheen.
Bird.Wood Pigeon: Large plump grey pigeon with white neck patches.
Bird.Starling: Dark, glossy bird that can sparkle green-purple and show pale speckles.
Bird.Crow: Large black bird with a strong dark bill; several crow species look similar.
Bird.Seagull: Gulls vary with age; look at size, beak and wing markings.
Bird.Parakeet: Bright green body, long pointed tail and red beak in a ring-necked parakeet.
Bird.Duck: Broad flat bill and webbed feet; plumage depends on species and sex.
Bird.Swan: Very large waterbird with a long neck; British mute swans usually have orange bills.
Bird.Owl: Rounded or heart-shaped face, forward-facing eyes and often silent flight.

Squirrel.Grey Squirrel: Usually grey-brown with a white belly and broad bushy tail.
Squirrel.Red Squirrel: Often russet red with a paler belly; some have ear tufts, especially in winter.
Squirrel.Flying Squirrel: Has a skin membrane between front and back legs for gliding; not native to Britain.
Squirrel.Ground Squirrel: Typically lives in burrows and spends more time on the ground.
Squirrel.Other Squirrel: Squirrels can be black, grey or reddish; colour alone does not prove species.

Rabbit.Wild Rabbit: Brown-grey coat, short fluffy tail and upright ears; lives in warrens.
Rabbit.Lop-eared: Domestic rabbit with ears that hang beside its face.
Rabbit.Dutch Rabbit: Domestic breed with clear patches of contrasting coat colour.
Rabbit.Lionhead: Domestic rabbit with a distinctive mane of longer fur around the head.
Rabbit.Netherland Dwarf: Small, compact pet rabbit with short ears.
Rabbit.Flemish Giant: Very large domestic rabbit with a long, sturdy body.

Hedgehog.European Hedgehog: Brown-and-cream spines, pointed face and small ears; native to Britain.
Hedgehog.African Pygmy Hedgehog: Smaller, often pale-faced pet hedgehog; not native to Britain.
Hedgehog.Long-eared Hedgehog: Has noticeably larger ears; native to parts of Asia and the Middle East.
Hedgehog.Other Hedgehog: Check face, ears and where it was seen before choosing a type.

Frog.Common Frog: Variable brown or olive skin with a dark patch behind the eye; found near ponds.
Frog.Pool Frog: Usually greenish-brown with spots; close identification can be difficult.
Frog.Marsh Frog: Large greenish frog with dark spots, often near water.
Frog.Tree Frog: Many have toe pads for climbing and bright green skin.
Frog.Bullfrog: Large frog with a broad head; not native to Britain.
Frog.Other Frog: Patterns vary a lot; a photo and the habitat are useful clues.

Other.Fox: Pointed muzzle, triangular ears and a long bushy tail.
Other.Deer: Hoofed mammal; size, antlers and rump pattern vary among deer species.
Other.Mouse: Small rodent with a pointed muzzle, whiskers and long thin tail.
Other.Bat: The only mammals capable of sustained powered flight; wings are skin membranes.
Other.Lizard: Scaly skin, long tail and usually four legs; some look snake-like.
Other.Worm: Long, soft segmented body; earthworms help mix and aerate soil.
Other.Slug: Soft shell-less-looking mollusc; often active in damp conditions.
Other.Fish: Fins and gills are key clues; look at body shape and fin placement.
Other.Tortoise: Land-dwelling reptile with a protective shell and stout legs.
Other.Other Animal: If it does not fit the groups, take a clear photo and add a description.
